svg.title: Turn lifecycle
svg.desc: A caller reserves a turn through TurnManager, which asks ExecutionCoordinator for an ExecutionLease and the primary runner for admission. TurnRunner then runs the pre-turn guard, composes the system prompt, starts limit timers and cost accounting, calls AgentHarness.turn, normalizes usage, runs the post-turn guard, persists the reply and frees the turn state. The coordinator releases the lease and the caller reads the TurnOutcome.
svg.text: One turn is 15 steps: admission and a lease before any provider work, one active turn per runner, and a settle phase that always runs.
caller side: admission, a lane permit, a lease, a turn id
TurnRunner, after executeTurn: deltas, tool use and results feed the buffer, SSE, loop detection and liveness
finally: a guard block, provider error, timeout or cancel jumps here
Step circle colour is the callee: green component, teal store, red guard.

g.title: Same-session reservations run one at a time in arrival order (SessionMutationCoordinator); the session's provider and execution policy are resolved here.
Lane choice, primary or worker. A fail-fast task or workflow request takes its permit before governance and skips governance when none is free.

Run on the primary runner for global governance. Order: read-only budget check, session lock (warn after 30 s, stuck after 120 s), then the two checks that record state; the lock is released if either fails.
g.text: admitTurnbudget, session lock, loop check, rate window

g.title: Permit from the primary or provider gate, then a cached compatible worker or a fresh one from provider wiring. The lease is released exactly once.
g.text: ExecutionLeasepermit, then a cached or new worker

g.title: On the leased runner. One active turn per runner, else BusyTurnException. The turn_state.json record is written synchronously.
GuardChain on the user message.
A non-empty per-turn override wins; otherwise the service composes the prompt for the turn's PromptScope.
The liveness tracker and wall-clock timer start; pending_accounting_turn_id is written before dispatch, and a failed write fails the turn with AccountingPersistenceException.
g.text: start limits and coststall + wall timers; session_cost pending

g.title: AgentHarness.turn. The harness's own timeout is the turn budget + 60 s, a crash backstop behind TurnRunner's timer.
Events arrive while the call runs.
Usage is normalized (Claude cumulative snapshot minus the session baseline), persisted in session_cost:<id>, and a one-shot context_warning fires at the threshold.
g.text: usage and contextdelta vs baseline; session_cost; ContextMonitor

g.title: GuardChain on the reply, evaluated unredacted, after usage was persisted.

Redaction applies when the reply is persisted. A failed or cancelled turn stores the partial buffer redacted, or [Turn cancelled] / [Turn failed]. Harnesses without a PreCompact hook get the heuristic pre-compaction flush.
g.text: persist replyMessageRedactor, insert; daily log if tools

g.title: Also clears the tool policy and timers, removes the active turn and releases the session lock; completes the outcome completer.
g.text: free turn statedelete turn_state record; TurnOutcome cached 30 s

g.title: The coordinator caches an idle healthy host worker, disposes task and workflow containers, and quarantines the permit when root-process exit is unconfirmed.
Returned from the retention cache when the turn already settled.
Caller. A web request, a channel, cron or a knowledge-inbox job. Tasks and workflow steps call ExecutionCoordinator.acquire directly.
TurnManager. Reserve, execute, cancel and outcome lookup across runners.
ExecutionCoordinator. Sole post-governance allocator.
TurnRunner. One harness's turn engine: guards, prompt, event stream, usage, persistence, limits, cancel.
Stores. session_cost:<id> in the KV store, session messages, and turn_state.json (TurnStateStore).
GuardChain. evaluateMessageReceived before the turn and evaluateBeforeAgentSend on the reply.
AgentHarness. turn() on the leased runner's harness; events stream back while it runs.
